title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated content was used to fabricate a false professional identity. Scammers created a fake social media advertisement using the likeness and identity of a real, named immigration attorney without his knowledge. The fraudulent persona was then used to solicit sensitive personal documents and repeated payments from a victim seeking immigration assistance. The failure occurred entirely outside any legitimate AI deployment, as a tool of deliberate deception rather than as a system gone wrong in production.

The mechanism that made the fraud effective was the AI's ability to produce convincing video and image content at scale. The real attorney reports that thousands of fake profiles and over eight thousand videos were created using his identity. This volume would have been difficult to achieve without automated content generation. The victim had no technical means at the point of contact to distinguish the AI-generated material from a genuine professional advertisement, and he discovered the fraud only through informal social trust, not through any platform or verification system.

What is not established is who the scammers are, whether any have been identified or charged, and whether the platforms that hosted the fraudulent advertisements took any action or bear any responsibility.

reports.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A Bronx legal resident lost $4,820 to scammers who used artificial intelligence and a fake social media ad to pose as an immigration attorney. Victor Hernandez, who has lived in the United States for over a decade after moving from the Dominican Republic, responded to an online ad promising citizenship help without taking the official exam. The scammers repeatedly requested personal documents and money through payment apps, claiming each new submission was necessary for processing. Hernandez only discovered the fraud when his wife expressed suspicion and they consulted a friend for help.

The fake ad was created using AI technology and based on real Miami immigration attorney Angel Leal's identity without his knowledge or permission. Leal reports that scammers have used his image to create thousands of fraudulent profiles targeting vulnerable immigrants across the country. He has spent considerable effort removing over 8,000 fake videos of himself and filed identity theft reports with the Florida bar. Leal advises potential clients to research attorneys thoroughly, meet them in person, and never pay through cash-sending apps. Hernandez, now facing eviction and unpaid utility bills, has filed reports with local and federal law enforcement agencies.
